display.exec: Neither reason nor systemMessage appears in exec JSON output.
display.tty: Both fields appear. The separate presentation probe records indented plain text under a branch prefix.
display.desktop: Reason appears. SystemMessage-only cases do not show their reply. Mixed cases show a reply card; the fields were not all reported separately.

answers.model: No START, MID or END reply marker appears in a captured CLI or desktop model request. A separate desktop model request contains the blocked prompt marker; its purpose was not retained.
answers.length: The CLI stream has START and END markers at every tested size. Desktop reason reaches the END marker and is copied byte for byte at the largest tested size. This establishes a tested bound, not the maximum limit.

text.markdown: Literal source in the interactive CLI and the desktop hook notice.
text.tty_bytes: The raw terminal stream does not contain the complete unmodified UTF-8 payload. It adds terminal formatting. Exact recovery from a terminal copy was not tested.
text.desktop_bytes: The copied DESK08 reason is byte for byte equal, including whitespace, Markdown, non-ASCII and astral characters. See its copy_checks for sizes and hashes.

form.tty: Indented hook output. See cli_presentation for the measured branch prefixes.
form.desktop: Hook blocked this message above an orange outline card. The reason inside is plain text.

answers.recommendation: Use block reason as an optional reply notice in interactive Codex and the desktop app. Keep view and the transcript tool for exec and a neutral reply display. Do not use systemMessage for desktop reply display. Do not claim that a command hook keeps tester prompts out of every model request.

source_inspection.method: Read the installed app.asar archive header and its JavaScript entries. Search the entries below for generateTitle, ThreadMetadataGenerationService, and thread_title. Store facts only, not app code or instructions.

version.runtime_cli_method: app-server thread/read metadata for the captured desktop session

facts: The desktop client has a ThreadMetadataGenerationService with generateTitle.
The title caller builds the title prompt from the submitted text.
The caller skips generation if the chat already has a non-provisional title.
The title generator uses the ephemeralGenerationModel and the thread_title feature.
The title request has a structured title and description response schema.
source_inspection.conclusion: Title generation is a candidate for the old side request. Its original schema and purpose were not retained. The new capture records a title-description schema match.

settings_search.method: Read the official config reference table with gstack browse. Search title, auxiliary, telemetry, background, hook and feedback. Also inspect codex features list and the desktop title caller.
settings_search.result: No verified setting to disable desktop chat title generation was found. tui.terminal_title controls the terminal title, not desktop chat title generation.
settings_search.init_and_trust_gate: Do not set an unverified key in init or the plugin. The trust gate cannot prove that the desktop sends no side request. Keep the documented limit until the harness provides a verified control.

cli.data: codex.cases in this file; each exec and tty case sends a first blocked prompt and then a passed prompt in the same conversation
cli.title_description_request: The old CLI captures did not retain schemas. No side request with a blocked-prompt marker was measured. Do not infer a guarantee from its absence.

side_request_investigation.conclusion: A Codex desktop title-generation request can contain a prompt blocked by UserPromptSubmit. No verified disable setting was found. State the limit; do not claim that the desktop relay keeps every tester prompt out of every model request.

summary.method: For each case, count whether any model_requests found map has its ID-PROMPT marker. A title request has title_description_schema true. Count reply markers ending in -reason-START or -reason-END the same way.
